Q1 · Scope and readiness
The problem

Water failures are hard to see and hard to follow up

Information
Buried in PDFs
The Department of Water and Sanitation audits every municipality each year, but the results sit in long PDF reports nobody can compare at a glance.
Residents
No clear way to report
A leak or an outage is reported by phone or social media. There is no reference number and no way to see if anyone acted.
Officials
No single view
Oversight staff cannot easily see which authorities are at risk, which fix-it plans are late, or which reports are still open.
169
water authorities across South Africa to keep an eye on, with the data spread over five reports and one Treasury website.

  • Blue Drop: drinking water, 0 to 100, higher is better. 95+ certified, 50 to 94 not certified, 31 to 49 poor, under 31 critical.

Q1 · Scope and readiness
The key term

What is a CAP?

Corrective Action Plan. When an authority is failing, it must write down what it will fix and by when. HydroSentinel tracks that promise.

Status
None
No plan yet. No deadline either.
→
Status
Submitted
A plan exists and has a deadline.
→
Status
In progress
Work has started.
→
Status
Completed
Work is finished.
Overdue rule
Deadline has passed and the plan is not completed. An authority with no plan can't be overdue, it has no deadline.
Where AI helps
The AI drafts 3 to 5 plan items with priorities and due dates. The official clicks Accept to apply one. Nothing changes before that.

Key pointsShow 10 s before the CAP demo step
  • CAP = Corrective Action Plan: what an authority will fix and by when.
  • Statuses: none, submitted, in progress, completed.
  • Overdue = deadline passed and not completed. No plan means no deadline, so never overdue.
  • AI drafts 3 to 5 items, a person clicks Accept. Nothing changes before that.

Q2 · Working prototype
Emerging technology · deep dive 1

How the risk model decides

1 · Inputs
Blue Drop, NRW*, maintenance %, CAP status, latitude, longitude. *no data loaded
→
2 · XGBoost
150 trees, depth 4. Gives a probability for low, medium, high
→
3 · Gate
Used only if the top class has 50%+ confidence
→
4 · Saved
Level, probability and source go to the score history
→
5 · Used
Map colour, high-risk alert, CAP priority
Fallback rule, used when
no model is loaded, or the Blue Drop score is missing (a made-up zero must never drive a prediction), or confidence is under 50%.
Rule: 35% low Blue Drop, 35% NRW (no data loaded, so it adds nothing), 20% low maintenance, plus CAP points. Crude: 34.5% accurate.
Where the labels came from
DWS Blue Drop Risk Rating for 144 authorities: 95 low, 32 medium, 17 high. The model learns an audited rating, not my opinion. Split stratified, fixed.
HydroSentinel13 / 36
Key pointsUse if asked "how does it work"
  • Keep it plain: numbers in, a probability out, a safety gate, then saved.
  • The history table records which source scored each run: XGBoost or the fallback rule.
  • Deployed model is retrained on all 144 rows. 89.7% comes from the earlier held-out experiment.
  • Code: backend/ai/predict.py, features.py, train.py.
Q2 · Working prototype
Emerging technology · deep dive 2 · how it predicts

How XGBoost predicts a risk level

1 · Inputs
Six numbers for one authority
Blue Drop score, NRW %, maintenance %, CAP status (0 to 3), latitude, longitude.
2 · Many small trees
150 trees, each at most 4 questions deep
Each tree asks yes/no questions about the numbers and ends in a score for low, medium and high. Boosting: every new tree is trained to fix the mistakes of the trees before it, adding only a small correction (learning rate 0.08).
3 · Add up
Scores become probabilities
The scores from the 150 trees are added per class and squashed so the three probabilities add to 100%.
4 · Gate
Highest class wins if it has 50% or more
Below 50%, or no Blue Drop score, the rule-based fallback scores it instead. The result and its source are saved.
Trained on 144 authorities with DWS risk labels (95 low, 32 medium, 17 high). 115 for training, 29 held back for testing. Settings: depth 4, subsample 0.9, learning rate 0.08.
HydroSentinel14 / 36
Key pointsUse when asked "how does it work"
  • Say: "Many small decision trees vote. Each one corrects the ones before it."
  • Probabilities come from multi:softprob: three numbers that add to 1. The top one is shown as the confidence.
  • The tree picture is an illustration. Say so. Real splits are learned.
  • Code: ai/train.py (settings), ai/predict.py (the 50% gate), ai/features.py (six inputs).

What the model relies on

How much each input is used by the trees (from the saved model)
Blue Drop score
41%
CAP status
19%
Maintenance %
16%
Longitude
13%
Latitude
12%
NRW %

Importance is how much each input improves the trees splits. It shows what the model uses, not what causes risk.
NRW has zero weight
The loaded data has no NRW values for any of the 169 authorities, so the input is always 0 and the model learned to ignore it. Fix: load the No Drop data.
Blue Drop leads
The DWS risk label is related to Blue Drop, so part of the accuracy is the model recovering that link.
CAP status and location
CAP status may follow risk, not cause it. Location is 25% combined and may be a regional proxy. Next: test without both.

Q2 · Working prototype
Emerging technology · deep dive 6

Say the weak points before they ask

Is 89.7% too good?
The DWS labels relate to Blue Drop, which is an input, so part of it is the model recovering a known link. Honest reading: it reproduces the DWS rating well. Value: covering authorities between audit cycles.
Only 29 test cases
One wrong answer moves accuracy 3.4 points. That is why cross-validation (80.6%, spread 8 points) is quoted next to it. Medium is the weakest class, 7 examples.
Location as an input
Risk clusters regionally, but with 144 rows the model may lean on geography. Next: test it without coordinates.
Only XGBoost tried
Compared to the fallback rule, not to other model families. Next: logistic regression and random forest.
Trend forecast
A straight line through score history. Simple statistics, I do not call it AI. It also mixes model and rule scores.
Photo check can be wrong
It flags, never decides. A photo cannot prove a report false.
HydroSentinel18 / 36
Key pointsKnow these cold
  • Markers reward saying a weakness before being caught.
  • Pattern: direct answer, why, the limit. Then stop.
  • If unsure: "I am not sure of the exact detail, but here is what I know." Never invent a number.
  • Full list of 71 answers in docs/a4/QA_PREP.md.

Question 2 · 2.3, 2.4 · Evidence slide

Real data and basic security

2.3 · Persistent, realistic data
169 real authorities from five DWS reports plus Treasury Municipal Money, loaded by an ETL pipeline into PostgreSQL (8 tables).

Duplicate spellings merged by a province + name key (115 duplicates removed).

Reports, scores, alerts and audit rows created in the demo persist across restarts. Photos on disk, path in the database.

Sample SQL ships in the repo for anyone who clones it.
2.4 · Security and reliability controls
Access: admin routes return 401 or 403 on the server.
Sessions: short JWT, single-use refresh token stored hashed, bcrypt passwords.
Credentials: keys in a git-ignored .env.
Personal data: public tracker returns status only, no location or description.
Uploads: images only.
AI abuse: 20 calls per admin per hour, 40 per visitor on public endpoints.
Safe failure: 503 or 502 for the AI feature only.
Accountability: append-only audit log.

Q2 · Working prototype
Question 2 · 2.3 · Backup slide

How the PDF data got in

1 · Sources
Five DWS PDFs and Treasury
Blue Drop, No Drop, Blue Drop Risk Rating, Green Drop (national and Gauteng), plus the Municipal Money website.
2 · Parse
One parser per source
Reads the PDF text with pdfplumber and text patterns. Each gives scores or bands per authority.
3 · Match
Same authority, one key
Province plus a cleaned name joins different spellings across reports.
4 · Load
Upsert into PostgreSQL
One row per authority in the WSA table. Missing numbers stay empty.
5 · Clean
Merge duplicates
A clean-up step merged 115 duplicate rows and left 169 authorities.

Q4 · Evidence
Limitations · 4:15 · 30 s

Three honest limits

1 · Silent fallback
Model once switched itself off
A wrong file path meant every authority used the weak rule (34.5%), and nothing showed it.
Fixed: it now warns and falls back to the bundled model. Next: show the scoring source in the admin page.
2 · Usage limit
Lives in memory
The 20-per-hour counter resets on restart and each server would count separately.
Fix: move the counter to a shared store such as Redis.
3 · Manual scoring
Started by hand
Risk is only re-scored when an admin asks. Scores go stale.
Fix: a scheduled job re-scores after every data load.

Also: accuracy rests on 29 test authorities, so one wrong answer moves it by 3.4 points.

Know your own decisions

Why XGBoost?
Small tabular data, handles missing values, beat the rule of thumb 89.7% to 34.5% on unseen data.
What if the AI is wrong?

How is it secured?
Login and refresh tokens, admin-only routes, hashed passwords, 20 AI calls an hour per admin, audit log.
What are the limits?
Counter in memory, scoring by hand, 29-case accuracy. Each has a fix.

Q5 · Presentation
Questions and answers · 1 of 5

Project and design

What is the central value?
It closes the loop between what residents experience and what regulators see: a report goes in, is triaged, linked to risk, turned into an action, and every step is recorded.
Why FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL?
FastAPI validates input from type definitions, which gives my 422 errors. React suits the many filters and tabs. PostgreSQL fits linked data and supports a JSON audit log. Familiar choices, not the only ones.
Show: backend/main.py, app/models.py
Why is the audit log append-only?
So it cannot be quietly changed. Each admin action adds a row: user, action, old value, new value. No code path edits or deletes a row.
Show: app/audit_helpers.py
Where does the business logic live?
Rules that matter (access, validation, alerts, scoring, audit) are on the back end so they cannot be bypassed. The front end does presentation: filters, paging, age badges.
Show: lib/reportAge.ts

Q5 · Presentation
Questions and answers · 2 of 5

The risk model

How accurate, and how do you know?
26 of 29 unseen authorities, 89.7%. The rule of thumb got 34.5%. Because 29 is small I also ran 5-fold cross-validation: 80.6%, plus or minus 8 points. I trust that figure more.
Isn't that too good? Could it be cheating?
Fair. Labels come from a DWS rating tied to Blue Drop, an input, so part is recovering a known link. The split is stratified and fixed, so no train and test leakage. Value is covering gaps between audits.
Why XGBoost?
It suits small tabular data, handles non-linear patterns, needs no scaling and is fast. I did not benchmark other families. That is a limit.
Show: ai/train.py
What if the model cannot be trusted?
It falls back to a rule when no model is loaded, the Blue Drop score is missing, or confidence is under 50%. The history records the source.
Show: ai/predict.py

Q5 · Presentation
Questions and answers · the risk model

XGBoost: likely questions

What is XGBoost in simple words?
Many small decision trees. Each new tree fixes the mistakes of the earlier ones. Together they give a probability for low, medium and high.
Why trees and not a neural network?
144 rows and six columns is small tabular data. Trees handle that well, need no scaling and are fast. A neural network would overfit.
What does "probability 0.83" mean?
The confidence in the top class, not a guaranteed real-world chance. I only use it above 50%, and I call it a confidence.
Why is NRW not used?
The loaded data has no NRW values for any authority, so the model gives it zero weight. Next: load the No Drop data and retrain.
Why does CAP status affect risk?
It is one of the six inputs, and the model found it useful. It may follow risk rather than cause it, so I would test the model without it.
Could it be overfitting with 144 rows?
Depth is limited to 4 and each tree sees 90% of rows. Cross-validation (80.6%, plus or minus 8) is the honest figure next to 89.7%.
How do you evaluate it?
Held-out 29 authorities: 26 right, 89.7%. A fixed split, stratified so each class appears. Plus 5-fold cross-validation. Rule of thumb: 34.5%.
Is the model retrained?
Offline, on demand: python -m ai.train_from_bdrr. The deployed model is trained on all 144 rows, so the 89.7% comes from the earlier split.
What would you improve?
Add NRW data, test without location and CAP status, compare against logistic regression and random forest, and re-score on a schedule.

Q5 · Presentation
Questions and answers · 3 of 5

GPT-4o and safety

How do you stop it making things up?
Prompts hold only real database values and are short. The CAP draft must be valid JSON citing a number. Most important: nothing the AI writes changes data until a person clicks Accept or Save.
What if OpenAI is down?
Clear errors: 503 with no key, 502 on failure. The rest of the system works. The map summary still shows live counts. I tested these cases.
Is the question agent safe?
It can only call fixed read-only tools, at most five rounds, no free SQL. It shows what it checked.
Show: ai/query_agent.py
How is cost controlled?
20 AI calls per admin per hour (429 after). Public AI endpoints 40 per visitor per hour. The digest is cached 24 hours.
Show: app/rate_limit.py

Q5 · Presentation
Questions and answers · 4 of 5

Data, security and privacy

Is the data real?
The 169 authorities and their indicators are real: five DWS reports plus Treasury Municipal Money. Reports are created during the demo or tests. Extracted rows ship as sample SQL.
Show: etl/run_etl.py
How does sign-in work?
Email and bcrypt password give a short JWT (about an hour) and a 7-day refresh token. Refresh tokens are stored hashed and single use. Admin routes return 401 or 403 on the server.
Show: app/auth.py
What are the security weaknesses?
Tokens in localStorage, no sign-in attempt limit, uploads checked by extension not content, and a default JWT secret that a real deployment must change.
Do you comply with POPIA?
I would not claim it. I collect no names, but free text and location can identify someone. The public tracker shows status only. A consent notice and retention policy are needed before real use, including for photos sent to OpenAI.
How do you load the PDFs?
A parser per report reads the PDF text with pdfplumber and patterns. A province plus cleaned-name key joins spellings, the rows are upserted, and a clean-up merged 115 duplicates. It runs offline, and the sample SQL ships in the repo.
Show: etl/run_etl.py, etl/name_matching.py
What data is missing?
NRW is empty for all 169 (the No Drop PDF has no NRW %). Maintenance has 120 values and Blue Drop 159. A missing Blue Drop score uses the fallback rule; other gaps are fed to the model as 0, which is a limit.
